description: Single worldwide repository of 3D structural data of large biological molecules such as proteins, nucleic acids, and complex assemblies, primarily from X-ray crystallography, NMR, and cryo-EM.
scale: 250,441 entries as of March 2026; ~17,000 new structures released annually in 2025
access_model: Fully open
one_line_hook: The world's first and foremost open archive of experimentally-determined 3D protein structures, powering decades of biomedical breakthroughs since 1971.
content_angles: AI vs experimental structure comparisons with AlphaFold
Drug design stories from PDB complexes

name: Global Terrorism Database (GTD)
operator: National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START), University of Maryland
description: Open-source database with systematic data on over 200,000 domestic, transnational, and international terrorist incidents worldwide from 1970-2020 (excl. 1993), including date/location, weapons, targets, casualties, perpetrators; derived from millions of media reports.GTD site
scale: >200,000 incidents (e.g., 210,454 per recent analysis), 1970-2020, >88k bombings, 19k assassinations, 11k kidnappingsGTD site
access_model: Free for non-commercial use (requires name/email/institution registration, EULA acceptance)[Terms](https://www.start.umd.edu/gtd/terms-of-use/)
one_line_hook: The world's most comprehensive unclassified database tracking 200k+ terrorist attacks since 1970.
adjacent_sources: RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents
Chicago Project on Security and Threats Suicide Attack Database
content_angles: 2. Rise of lone-wolf vs. group attacks
3. Regional hotspots (e.g., Sahel, Middle East) and policy implications.

name: Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)
operator: NHTSA (National Highway Traffic Safety Administration)
domain: Transportation safety / Motor vehicle crash data
description: Nationwide census of police-reported fatal motor vehicle traffic crashes in the US (50 states, DC, Puerto Rico), including details on crashes, vehicles, persons, factors like impairment, seatbelts, and road conditions.
scale: Annual data 1975-present (~40,000-43,000 fatal crashes/year recently; e.g., 37,654 crashes & 40,901 fatalities in 2023; cumulative millions of records)
access_model: Free public access via web query tools ([FARS Encyclopedia](https://www-fars.nhtsa.dot.gov)), FTP downloads ([ftp.nhtsa.dot.gov/FARS](ftp://ftp.nhtsa.dot.gov/FARS)), and API
one_line_hook: Unlock 50 years of US fatal crash data to reveal hidden patterns in America's deadliest roads.
content_angles: 1. Tech vs Lives: AVs & impairment tech saving X thousands?
3. State Shame: Top/bottom fatality states & policies

name: National UFO Reporting Center (NUFORC)
operator: Non-profit corporation operated by Peter Davenport (director)
description: Online database of public-submitted UFO/UAP sighting reports including date, location, shape, duration, summary, and full text descriptions, browsable by date, state/country, shape, and posting date
scale: ~170,000 reports since 1974 (147,890 as of Jan 2024 scrape; >2,000 in first half of 2025)
data_formats: Web pages/HTML; scraped to CSV/JSON by third parties (no official bulk download)
access_model: Fully open (public website browsing)
one_line_hook: World's largest independent archive of 170k+ UFO sightings since 1974, actively collecting reports via hotline and web form
seed_accuracy_note: Accurate: ~150,000+ sightings since 1974 per multiple sources including Wikipedia and site itself

name: Global Volcanism Program
operator: Smithsonian Institution, Department of Mineral Sciences, National Museum of Natural History
description: Catalog of Holocene volcanoes (last 12,000 years) and their eruptions, including physical characteristics, eruptive histories, current activity reports, and related data from scientific sources and observatories.
scale: 1,222 Holocene volcanoes; thousands of eruptions; 40-50 ongoing eruptions typically; weekly/daily reports.
access_model: Fully open
one_line_hook: The definitive global catalog tracking Earth's volcanic eruptions for 12,000 years, updated weekly with real-time crisis monitoring.
adjacent_sources: WOVOdat (volcanic unrest); USGS Volcano Hazards Program databases; NOAA/NCEI Global Volcano Locations (derived from GVP).
content_angles: Historical mega-eruptions and their global impacts
Volcano forecasting using 50+ years of data patterns.

name: Wayback Machine
operator: Internet Archive, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
last_updated: Ongoing; reached 1 trillion pages in Oct 2025 [Archivarix](https://archivarix.com/en/blog/webarchive-2026/)
description: Digital archive of the World Wide Web allowing users to view historical versions of websites from as early as 1996.
scale: Over 1 trillion web pages, ~100 petabytes of data web.archive.org, Archivarix
access_model: Free public web interface; download available for some data
api_available: Yes: Availability API, CDX Server API, Memento [archive.org/help/wayback_api.php](https://archive.org/help/wayback_api.php)
one_line_hook: The internet's ultimate time machine: 1+ trillion pages preserved since 1996.
viral_potential: High - Nostalgic "see how [site] looked in 1999" shares, lost media discoveries.
visual_potential: High - Side-by-side then/now website screenshots, evolution timelines.
content_angles: 3. Battles over access (e.g., lawsuits, AI scraping).

name: Macaulay Library
operator: Cornell Lab of Ornithology (Cornell University)
last_updated: Ongoing (recent uploads visible as of 2026; 470k new audio in 2024)
domain: Wildlife media archive (audio, photos, video of birds and other animals)
description: Scientific archive containing photos, audio recordings, and videos of birds (10,056 species), amphibians, fish, mammals, and more (2,674 species).
scale: 93.7 million total media items (89.9M photos, 3.4M audio, 425k video); 80k contributors; used in 1,427 publications.
data_formats: Metadata as CSV export; raw audio (e.g. WAV)
video via request/download for own media.
access_model: Partial (view/listen online free; raw files via request for research/education, license for commercial)
one_line_hook: World's largest archive of wildlife audio since 1929, with millions of bird calls and growing non-bird collections.
content_angles: Rare species sounds, recording milestones (e.g. 2024 best-of), conservation research using archive, contributor stories, tech like Merlin Sound ID.
seed_accuracy_note: Accurate; focuses on animal (primarily bird) sound recordings as described.
